simple.meaning: חֲרֵי־יוֹנִים (chărêy-yôwnîym) is a Hebrew word meaning “excrements of doves.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חֲרֵי־יוֹנִים (H2755) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Kings 6:25, with occurrences in 2 Kings.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֲרֵי־יוֹנִים (H2755) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חֲרֵי־יוֹנִים (H2755) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חֲרֵי־יוֹנִים (chărêy-yôwnîym) / H2755 is traced through 2 Kings 6:25, 2 Kings 18:27 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.rootNote: from the plural of 2716 and the plural of 3123 ; or perhaps rather the plural of a single word חֲרָאיוֹן , probably a kind of vegetable

occurrences.englishText: There was a great famine in Samaria. Behold, they besieged it, until a donkey’s head was sold for eighty pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a kab* A kab was about 2 liters, so a fourth of a kab would be about 500 milliliters or about a pint of dove’s dung for five pieces of silver.

But Rabshakeh said to them, “Has my master sent me to your master and to you, to speak these words? Hasn’t he sent me to the men who sit on the wall, to eat their own dung, and to drink their own urine with you?”
